title: OSHA crane operator training, certification and evaluation practice questions
description: Free practice questions on OSHA crane operator training, certification and evaluation (29 CFR 1926.1427), each answer quoted from the rule.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1427(a)(2), which operators are not required to comply with § 1926.1427?

options.A: Operators of tower cranes with a fixed working boom
options.B: Operators of derricks, sideboom cranes, or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less
options.C: Operators of crawler cranes used only for material handling
options.D: Operators who have held a crane operator job for more than 5 years

questions.explanation: 1926.1427(a)(2) says "Operators of derricks (see § 1926.1436), sideboom cranes (see § 1926.1440), or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less (see § 1926.1441) are not required to comply with § 1926.1427." Its note adds: "The training requirements in those other sections continue to apply".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For the U.S. military qualification in 1926.1427(a)(3), who counts as an employee of the U.S. military?

options.A: Any employee of a private contractor working on a military base
options.B: Any veteran who operated cranes while in the service
options.C: Any employee of a private contractor holding a Department of Defense contract
options.D: A Federal employee of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces, not employees of private contractors

questions.explanation: "An employee of the U.S. military is a Federal employee of the Department of Defense or Armed Forces and does not include employees of private contractors."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1926.1427(a)(3)(ii)(A) says a U.S. military operator qualification is "Not portable." What does that mean under the rule?

options.A: It meets paragraph (a) only where the operator is employed by (and operating the equipment for) the employer that issued the qualification
options.B: It may be used with any construction employer for 5 years
options.C: It is valid only on Federal construction projects
options.D: It must be converted into a State license before use

questions.explanation: The qualification is "Not portable: Such a qualification meets the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section only where the operator is employed by (and operating the equipment for) the employer that issued the qualification." It is "Valid for the period of time stipulated by the issuing entity."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1427(a)(1), how may an employee who has not been certified/licensed and evaluated operate assigned equipment covered by 1926.1427?

options.A: Freely during the first 90 days after hire
options.B: Freely whenever a signal person is present
options.C: Only as an operator-in-training under supervision in accordance with paragraph (b)
options.D: Only after a competent person signs a daily permit

questions.explanation: Such an employee "may only operate the equipment as an operator-in-training under supervision in accordance with the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1926.1427(b)(3)(v) lets an uncertified operator-in-training work in multiple-lift rigging operations in one case. What is it?

options.A: Where the operator's trainer determines that the operator-in-training's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work
options.B: Where the lift is planned by a competent person
options.C: Where a qualified rigger approves the lift in writing
options.D: Where the operator-in-training has completed 6 months of training

questions.explanation: The operator-in-training may not operate "In multiple-lift rigging operations, except where the operator's trainer determines that the operator-in-training's skills are sufficient for this high-skill work."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1926.1427(b)(3)(i) bars an uncertified operator-in-training from operating when equipment could get within a set distance of a power line. What distance does it set for a power line that is over 350 kV?

options.A: 10 feet
options.B: 50 feet
options.C: 20 feet
options.D: 100 feet

questions.explanation: The operator-in-training may not operate if any part of the equipment, load line, or load "could get within 20 feet of a power line that is up to 350 kV, or within 50 feet of a power line that is over 350 kV."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1427(b)(4)(iii), what must the operator's trainer and the operator-in-training do when the equipment is a tower crane?

options.A: Sit together in the operator's cab
options.B: Communicate only through a dedicated signal person
options.C: Stay within 20 feet of each other
options.D: Be in direct communication with each other

questions.explanation: "For tower cranes: The operator's trainer and the operator-in-training must be in direct communication with each other." For other equipment they "must be in direct line of sight of each other."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: 1926.1427(b)(4)(iv) allows short breaks in the trainer's monitoring when all of its conditions are met. Which of these is one of those conditions?

options.A: A signal person takes over monitoring during the break
options.B: The break is recorded in a written log
options.C: Immediately prior to the break, the trainer informs the operator-in-training of the specific tasks to perform and the limitations to follow
options.D: The operator-in-training lowers every load to the ground for the whole break

questions.explanation: "Immediately prior to the break the operator's trainer informs the operator-in-training of the specific tasks that the operator-in-training is to perform and limitations to which he/she must adhere during the operator trainer's break." The tasks must also be "within the operator-in-training's abilities."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1926.1427(b)(5) require the employer to provide retraining to an operator?

options.A: Every 3 years on a fixed schedule
options.B: Only when the operator's certification is renewed
options.C: Only after an OSHA inspection finds a violation
options.D: When, based on the operator's performance or an evaluation of the operator's knowledge, there is an indication that retraining is necessary

questions.explanation: "The employer must provide retraining in relevant topics for each operator when, based on the performance of the operator or an evaluation of the operator's knowledge, there is an indication that retraining is necessary."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1427(c)(1), when must an equipment operator be licensed by a state or local government?

options.A: When that government issues operator licenses for equipment covered under subpart CC and its licensing program meets the requirements of (c)(1), for operation within its jurisdiction
options.B: In every State, whether or not the State issues crane licenses
options.C: Only on publicly funded projects
options.D: Only when the operator lacks a certification from an accredited testing organization

questions.explanation: "When a state or local government issues operator licenses for equipment covered under subpart CC, the equipment operator must be licensed by that government entity for operation of equipment within that entity's jurisdiction if that government licensing program meets the following requirements".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1427(c)(3), who bears the cost when operator certification/licensure is required?

options.A: The operator, who pays the testing fee
options.B: The employer, who must provide it at no cost to employees
options.C: The operator and employer split the cost
options.D: The controlling entity on the project

questions.explanation: "Whenever operator certification/licensure is required under this section, the employer must provide the certification/licensure at no cost to employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1427(d)(1)(ii)(B), on what basis must the tests of an accredited crane operator testing organization provide certification?

options.A: Capacity alone
options.B: The employer's project location
options.C: Equipment type, or type and capacity
options.D: The operator's years of experience

questions.explanation: The organization must administer written and practical tests that "Provide certification based on equipment type, or type and capacity."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: If no accredited testing agency offers a certification examination for a particular type of equipment, how does 1926.1427(d)(2) let the operator comply?

options.A: By being evaluated by the employer only, with no certification
options.B: By operating as an operator-in-training indefinitely
options.C: By obtaining a letter from the equipment manufacturer
options.D: By being certified for the type that is most similar to that equipment and for which an examination is available, with the certificate stating the type

questions.explanation: The operator "will be deemed to have complied with the certification requirements of this section for that equipment if the operator has been certified for the type that is most similar to that equipment and for which a certification examination is available. The operator's certificate must state the type of equipment for which the operator is certified."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which certification does 1926.1427 describe as "portable among employers who are required to have operators certified under this option"?

options.A: A certification by an accredited crane operator testing organization under paragraph (d)
options.B: A certification from an audited employer program under paragraph (e)
options.C: A U.S. military operator qualification under paragraph (a)(3)
options.D: An employer's evaluation document under paragraph (f)(6)

questions.explanation: Under (d)(3), "A certification issued under this option is portable among employers who are required to have operators certified under this option." Audited-program certificates and military qualifications are both described as "Not portable".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In an audited employer program, the written and practical tests may be approved by an auditor under 1926.1427(e)(1)(ii). Which auditor meets that paragraph?

options.A: The employer's own competent person
options.B: One certified to evaluate such tests by an accredited crane operator testing organization who is not an employee of the employer
options.C: Any employee of the employer with 10 years of crane experience
options.D: A representative of the equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: "The auditor is certified to evaluate such tests by an accredited crane operator testing organization" and "The auditor is not an employee of the employer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When the auditor determines there is a significant deficiency in an audited employer program, who files the documented report of the deficiency with the appropriate OSHA Regional Office under 1926.1427(e)(5)(iii)?

options.A: The employer
options.B: The operator
options.C: The accredited crane operator testing organization
options.D: The auditor

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure that "The auditor files a documented report of the deficiency to the appropriate Regional Office of the Occupational Safety and Health Administration within 15 days of the auditor's determination that there is a deficiency."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which item must the employer's document of a completed evaluation provide under 1926.1427(f)(6)?

options.A: The weights of every load lifted during the evaluation
options.B: The operator's certification card number
options.C: The make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation
options.D: The name of the operator's training school

questions.explanation: The document must provide "The operator's name; the evaluator's name and signature; the date; and the make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1926.1427(f)(3) say about a certificate or degree for the evaluation in paragraph (f)(1)?

options.A: A crane operator certificate replaces the evaluation
options.B: Possession of a certificate or degree cannot, by itself, cause a person to be qualified for purposes of (f)(1)
options.C: A degree in engineering replaces the evaluation
options.D: A certificate counts as the evaluation for 5 years

questions.explanation: "The definition of “qualified” in § 1926.32 does not apply to paragraph (f)(1) of this section: Possession of a certificate or degree cannot, by itself, cause a person to be qualified for purposes of paragraph (f)(1)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Language, certification criteria and effective dates
questions.question: Under 1926.1427(h)(2), which equipment may an operator certified through a test given in a particular language operate?

options.A: Only equipment furnished with the materials required by the subpart, such as operations manuals and load charts, written in the language of the certification
options.B: Any equipment, if a translator is on site
options.C: Only equipment whose controls are labeled in English
options.D: Any equipment, once the employer's evaluation is complete

questions.explanation: "The operator is only permitted to operate equipment that is furnished with materials required by this subpart, such as operations manuals and load charts, that are written in the language of the certification."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1427, Operator training, certification, and evaluation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Language, certification criteria and effective dates
questions.question: What effective date does 1926.1427(k)(2) set for the evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f)?

options.A: December 10, 2018
options.B: November 9, 2018
options.C: February 7, 2019
options.D: August 9, 2010

questions.explanation: "The evaluation and documentation requirements in paragraphs (a) and (f) are effective on February 7, 2019." The rest of the section is "effective on December 10, 2018."
